title: Cross Game
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ko Kitamura grows up beside the four Tsukishima sisters, and Wakaba, born the same day as him, treats him as her boyfriend. After Wakaba drowns in fifth grade, Ko quietly trains to fulfil her dream of seeing him pitch at Koshien, the national high-school championship, while her sister Aoba, a gifted pitcher who resents him, slowly grows closer to him. A sports and coming-of-age story with an understated touch.
life_message: Honor those you lose by quiet, faithful effort, and let shared work with friends heal grief.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes settled by a decisive game, not personal feuds (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Team discipline and training valued, with personal choice.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Coaches and school rank matter, though the home team challenges them (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern secular setting with strong custom of Koshien.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Hard work and promises outrank self-expression.

folkways.japan: Koshien, the national high-school baseball tournament, is a deep Japanese tradition, and the reserved, unspoken expression of grief and love reflects Japanese norms of restraint.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia cites praise for silent scenes and an elliptical style that convey the message without dialogue.

personified.character: Interim principal and imported head coach
personified.ideology: winning by recruiting elite outsiders over the home-grown team

delivery.note: The elite first-string program loses and its adults leave, yet its star player stays and joins Ko's circle.

winners_losers: Ko's patient home-grown team and Wakaba's memory win; the win-by-recruitment approach loses, though its star player is welcomed.
